newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot restarts Moscow-Riga route Nov 22.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot restarts Moscow-Riga route Nov 22.

text.p: Russia's flagship international carrier Aeroflot will resume regular flights between Moscow and the Latvian capital Riga from November 22, an airline official said on Wednesday.
Leonid Mokhov, deputy head of Aeroflot's Commonwealth of Independent States and Baltics department, told Reuters that Latvian aviation authorities had confirmed the Russian carrier's winter schedule.

"It means that we have permission to resume regular flights," he said, adding that Aeroflot held talks with Latvian aviation officials without the participation of the Russian Federal Aviation Service.
Aeroflot ceased flights to Riga on October 31 after the Latvian transport ministry refused to confirm its winter schedule.
Latvia said it was a response to Russia's refusal to allow Air Baltic to fly to Moscow, because the Latvian carrier owed $2.8 million for airport services.

A Latvian transport official said earlier on Tuesday that Latvia had given Aeroflot permission to resume the flights and was confident its debt problem could be sorted out, allowing it to resume its own Moscow flights.
Mokhov said that Aeroflot would make scheduled flights on Tuesdays, Fridays and Sundays operating a Tupolev-134 jet. "It is a promising route for us," he added.
Another Russian carrier -- privately-owned Transaero -- flies between Moscow and Riga under a code-sharing agreement with Latvia's private RiAir airline.
